refnamediv.refpurpose: SUNDIALS ordinary differential equation symplectic Runge-Kutta solver

refsynopsisdiv.title: Syntax
refsynopsisdiv.synopsis: [t,y] = sprkode(f1,f2,tspan,y0,<opt_args>) [t,y,info] = sprkode(f1,f2,tspan,y0,<opt_args>) sol = sprkode(...) solext = sprkode(sol,tfinal,<opt_args>) sprkode(...)

listitem.para: a function, a string or a list, the right hand side(s) of the differential equation
double vector, time interval or time points

a sequence of optional named arguments, see the solvers options

refsection.title: Description
refsection.para: sprk computes the solution of Hamiltonian systems posed under the form

para.latex: p' = f_1(t,q)=\frac{\partial V(t,q)}{\partial q},~q'=f_2(t,p)=\frac{\partial T(t,p)}{\partial p}.

refsection.para: allowing for conservation of quadratic invariants (sprkode uses a symplectic integrator).

At the user level, when the dimension of the generalized momentum p and coordinates q is n then the right hand side functions f1(t,y) and f2(t,y) are called with a vector of size 2*n and the partition of y is arbitrary chosen by the user when defining the initial conditions. Then in the output of f1 the components of q' must be set to zero, as well as the the components of p' output of f2 (see the example below).
As time adaptivity destroys the conservation properties, this solver must be used with a fixed step, hence the sequence of options must set the fixedStep option.

As sprkode shares with arkode most of its features (syntax, specification of user functions) please refer to the Description section of arkode help page for basic usage (events handling, solution output, callback).

refsection.title: Example
refsection.para: In the following example, we solve the harmonic oscilator Hamiltonian system.

para.scilab:image:
function dpdt = f1(t,pq) q = pq(2); dpdt = [-q; 0]; end function dqdt = f2(t,pq) p = pq(1); dqdt = [0; p] end
[t,pq] = sprkode(f1,f2, [0 20], [1;0], fixedStep = 0.1)
subplot(1,2,1) plot(pq(1,:),pq(2,:)) xlabel("$p$") ylabel("$q$") isoview("on") subplot(1,2,2) plot(t,sum(pq.^2,1)) gca().data_bounds(3:4) = [0.9,1.1]; xlabel("t") ylabel("$p^2+q^2$") title("energy") gcf().figure_size=[640 410]
